sections.body:
### Exercise 1 — Add an `update_event` tool

Extend the Calendar Agent with `update_event(event_id: int, title: str | None = None, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None)` that updates only the provided fields.

<details>
<summary>Solution</summary>

```python
from datetime import datetime
from pydantic_ai import Agent

@calendar.tool_plain
def update_event(event_id: int, title: str | None = None, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Update an existing event. Only fields you pass will change.

    Args:
        event_id: The ID of the event to update.
        title: New title, or omit to keep current.
        start: New ISO 8601 start, or omit to keep current.
        end: New ISO 8601 end, or omit to keep current.
    """
    if event_id not in events_db:
        return f"No event with ID {event_id}."
    e = events_db[event_id]
    if title is not None:
        e["title"] = title
    if start is not None:
        e["start"] = datetime.fromisoformat(start)
    if end is not None:
        e["end"] = datetime.fromisoformat(end)
    return f"Updated event #{event_id}: {e['title']}"

print(calendar.run_sync(
    "Add 'Lunch with Pat' 2025-03-10 12:00 to 13:00, then rename it to 'Lunch with Patrice' and extend to 14:00."
).data)
```

Optional parameters become non-required fields in the JSON schema, so the LLM only fills in fields the user mentioned.

</details>

### Exercise 2 — Tag events and add `find_by_tag`

Add a `tags: list[str]` field to events, accept tags in `add_event`, and add a `find_by_tag(tag: str)` tool.

<details>
<summary>Solution</summary>

```python
from datetime import datetime
from pydantic_ai import Agent

@calendar.tool_plain
def add_event(title: str, start: str, end: str, tags: list[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Add a new calendar event.

    Args:
        title: Short human-readable title.
        start: ISO 8601 start datetime.
        end: ISO 8601 end datetime.
        tags: Optional list of tags (e.g. ['work', 'important']).
    """
    eid = next_id["v"]
    next_id["v"] += 1
    events_db[eid] = {
        "id": eid,
        "title": title,
        "start": datetime.fromisoformat(start),
        "end": datetime.fromisoformat(end),
        "tags": tags or [],
    }
    return f"Created event #{eid}: {title} (tags: {tags or []})"

@calendar.tool_plain
def find_by_tag(tag: str) -> str:
    """List all events that have the given tag (case-insensitive)."""
    t = tag.lower()
    hits = [e for e in events_db.values() if t in [x.lower() for x in e.get("tags", [])]]
    if not hits:
        return f"No events tagged '{tag}'."
    return "\n".join(f"#{e['id']} {e['title']}" for e in hits)

print(calendar.run_sync(
    "Add 'Standup' 2025-03-07 09:00-09:30 tagged work and daily. "
    "Then list everything tagged 'work'."
).data)
```

</details>

### Exercise 3 — Add `export_to_json` to the note agent

Add a `@note_agent.tool` named `export_to_json` that calls `ctx.deps.all_json()` and returns the string. Verify it works after saving two notes.

<details>
<summary>Solution</summary>

```python
from pydantic_ai import RunContext

@note_agent.tool
def export_to_json(ctx: RunContext[NotesDB]) -> str:
    """Export all saved notes as a JSON string. Use when the user asks to download or back up notes."""
    return ctx.deps.all_json()

# Test
db = NotesDB()
note_agent.run_sync("Save 'hello world' tagged test.", deps=db)
note_agent.run_sync("Save 'second note' tagged test.", deps=db)
print(note_agent.run_sync("Export all my notes as JSON.", deps=db).data)
```

The agent's final answer will include the JSON in its text response. In production, you might return a download URL instead.

</details>
